tasks.short: Check supplier and staffing agency invoices and get approved payments ready in AFAS.

today.trigger: An invoice arrives in Outlook, AFAS or a staffing agency portal; the payment run approaches.
steps: Collect the invoice and check supplier details, invoice number, VAT and possible duplicates.
Compare charges with the purchase approval, delivery evidence or approved agency hours and rates.
Check the AFAS booking and ask the site manager or bookkeeper to resolve differences.
Prepare approved invoices for the payment batch and obtain the required authorisations.
Check payment status against Rabobank records and file supporting evidence.
drudgery: Downloading agency invoices and hours files.
Comparing invoice lines with approved hours and rate tables.
Chasing missing approvals and attachments.
today.time_sinks: Assumed workflow: most effort sits in exceptions, missing approvals and agency rate differences; actual volumes and touch times are unknown.

lenses.faster: Extract invoice fields once and run duplicate, VAT and matching checks automatically. The accountant receives a short list of differences with the supporting documents attached.
lenses.autonomous: Invoice receipt starts checking and approval routing without a reminder. The workflow prepares a batch only from invoices that have passed the required approvals.
lenses.ambitious: Check every agency invoice against approved hours, contracted rates and applicable allowances. Show repeated errors by agency and site so Finance can fix the cause.
lenses.joy: Remove portal downloads, copying fields and routine chasing. Keep supplier disputes, unusual charges and decisions that need commercial judgment.
lenses.options: Compare payment dates against due dates, available discounts and the cash forecast. Present the cost and cash effect of each permitted schedule.
lenses.altitude: Own invoice control rules, exception thresholds and supplier data quality. Improve the percentage of invoices processed without touch.
reach: Bookkeeper: routine invoice matching and approval follow-up.
Controller: analysis of agency billing errors and recurring control failures.
FP&A Analyst: confirmed supplier payment inputs for the cash forecast.

tasks.human_edge: Resolve disputed charges, interpret unusual contractual terms and recognise suspicious supplier changes. Authorised people retain payment release responsibility.
tasks.pattern_why: Use llm_step for invoice extraction and deterministic_software for arithmetic, duplicates and matching. Payment preparation spans several systems, so approval is required before the batch proceeds.

in_practice.trigger: A new invoice enters the controlled intake queue, or the scheduled payment run starts.
steps: Retrieve the invoice through an approved connector or controlled import and retain the original.
Extract fields with source references, validate totals and apply duplicate and VAT checks.
Match against approved purchases or agency hours and versioned contract rates.
Route differences and missing approvals to named owners; prepare only approved items.
Present the proposed AFAS batch for authorisation and reconcile returned bank status.
in_practice.human_gate: Budget owners approve charges; the accountant reviews exceptions and the proposed batch. Authorised bank signatories release payments under the existing separation of duties; bank-detail changes require independent verification.
systems: Staffing agency portals or controlled exports
data_needed: Supplier master data and approved bank details.
Original invoices, purchase approvals and delivery evidence.
Approved agency hours and effective contract rates, including agreed allowance treatment.
VAT rules, approval limits, due dates and payment permissions.
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS invoice and approval records, with a restricted SharePoint evidence register recording checks, exceptions, authorisations and batch references.

evidence.claim: Structured invoice matching, duplicate detection and approval routing can use explicit rules; document extraction can supply fields for validation.
The proposed workflow could save 65% of accountant handling time and make completion twice as fast; these are untested estimates for Noordhaven.

risks: False matches or incorrect allowance rules can approve overbilling; use approved hours and contracted agency rates rather than assuming employee CAO rates apply directly.
Supplier bank-detail fraud and duplicate payments require controls independent of document extraction.
Agency files contain personal data; restrict fields, access and retention under AVG/GDPR.
Portal exports, AFAS imports and Rabobank batch interfaces may require manual steps or additional integration work.
research_questions: What share of accountant time concerns routine invoices versus exceptions already escalated by the bookkeepers?
Can all three agencies provide stable invoice and approved-hours exports with matching identifiers?
Which approvals and bank controls must remain manual, and how much elapsed time do they add?
Does a shadow pilot catch known duplicate, rate and VAT errors without excessive false alerts?

tasks.short: Check our financial records and close reports for missing items, errors and reporting compliance.

today.trigger: A close milestone, reporting deadline or unexpected financial movement requires a review.
steps: Export AFAS balances and transactions and collect supporting schedules.
Check completeness, cut-off, account movements and agreement between reports and the ledger.
Compare presentation and accounting treatment with the approved reporting policies.
Investigate differences with bookkeepers, payroll and site owners.
Prepare a reviewed report and retain evidence of checks and corrections.
drudgery: Rebuilding check sheets and copying ledger totals.
Searching for explanations and supporting documents.
Repeating the same completeness and consistency checks.
today.time_sinks: Assumed workflow: assembling a consistent reporting pack and investigating unexplained movements consume much of the review time.

lenses.faster: Build the report from a controlled AFAS extract and run the standard checks together. Draft explanations only where a movement or failed check needs attention.
lenses.autonomous: A completed extract starts completeness checks and produces a review pack. Failed checks create assigned exceptions instead of waiting for someone to notice them.
lenses.ambitious: Run selected close checks throughout the month across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo. Give the business earlier warning of cost omissions and unreliable forecast inputs.
lenses.joy: Remove report assembly and repetitive ticking of balances. Keep the investigation of unusual transactions and the explanation of what changed.
lenses.options: Compare materiality thresholds and show alternative treatments for uncertain items. Separate confirmed facts from assumptions and show their effect on the statements.
lenses.altitude: Design the reporting controls and decide what evidence is enough. Track which checks prevent audit adjustments and shorten the close.
reach: Controller: first review of site financial packs.
FP&A Analyst: reconciled actuals and evidence-backed variance explanations.
Bookkeeper: identification of missing or inconsistent postings.

tasks.human_edge: Judge materiality, accounting policy and whether an explanation is credible. The accountant remains responsible for the conclusions presented to the Controller.
tasks.pattern_why: deterministic_software can test balances and completeness, while llm_step can draft explanations from cited evidence. Assessing reporting conformance and accepting the final report require professional review.

in_practice.trigger: A versioned AFAS reporting extract is available or a close review is requested.
steps: Capture the period, extraction timestamp, ledger control totals and applicable reporting policies.
Run approved balance, cut-off, completeness and report-to-ledger checks.
Collect evidence for exceptions and draft explanations with transaction references.
Present failed checks, uncertain treatments and proposed corrections in a review pack.
After accountant approval, publish the pack and retain its data and policy versions.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant resolves material exceptions and approves conclusions; the Controller signs off the close pack under the existing reporting responsibilities.
data_needed: Trial balance, transaction detail and subledger control totals.
Close checklist, accounting policies and materiality thresholds.
Prior-period comparisons and supporting schedules.
Extract timestamps, corrections and named account owners.
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint close folders containing versioned check results, transaction references, review decisions and the approved report.

evidence.claim: Ledger consistency checks can be automated, and language models can draft explanations from supplied accounting evidence subject to review.
A 55% handling-time reduction and twofold completion speed are pilot assumptions, not measured results.

risks: A nightly Power BI extract can omit late postings; reports must identify their data timestamp and tie to the chosen ledger snapshot.
Plausible narrative can conceal unsupported explanations or incorrect accounting treatment.
Checks cannot find omitted transactions without independent completeness evidence.
Payroll detail should be limited to what the review needs and protected under AVG/GDPR.
research_questions: Which reporting framework and internal accounting policies apply to each required report?
Which past audit adjustments would the proposed checks have detected?
Can every report be reproduced from a frozen extract with matching ledger control totals?
How much review effort remains after pack preparation is automated?

tasks.short: Reconcile bank, payroll, agency and ledger balances and explain the differences.

today.trigger: The month closes, a new bank statement arrives or an account has an unexplained balance.
steps: Collect AFAS transactions, bank statements and relevant payroll or agency control totals.
Match entries using references, amounts and dates.
List unmatched items and distinguish timing differences from errors.
Obtain evidence and prepare proposed corrections or follow-up actions.
Approve the reconciliation and carry unresolved items into the next review.
drudgery: Matching rows across spreadsheets.
Rechecking old outstanding items.
Copying evidence into reconciliation files.
today.time_sinks: Assumed workflow: inconsistent references, split payments and unresolved items drive the manual matching and follow-up.

lenses.faster: Match exact references and approved split-payment patterns automatically. Show only residual differences with their history and supporting records.
lenses.autonomous: Each bank import or ledger extract refreshes the reconciliation and ages unresolved items. Routine matches complete without intervention; proposed corrections wait for approval.
lenses.ambitious: Reconcile high-risk accounts daily and cover every balance-sheet account on a defined schedule. Spot recurring payroll, agency and cash differences before month-end.
lenses.joy: Remove row matching and repeated searches for old explanations. Keep tracing unusual differences and fixing the underlying process.
lenses.options: For ambiguous matches, show several candidates with the evidence for each. Compare waiting for a timing difference to clear with investigating or correcting it now.
lenses.altitude: Own reconciliation coverage, matching rules and unresolved-item limits. Use exception patterns to improve upstream data quality.
reach: Bookkeeper: routine bank and subledger matching.
Payroll Specialist: reconciliation of payroll totals to ledger postings.
Credit and Collections Officer: identification of unapplied customer cash.

tasks.human_edge: Distinguish genuine timing differences from errors, fraud or missing liabilities. Approve corrections and decide when an outstanding item needs escalation.
tasks.pattern_why: Most matching uses structured amounts, references and explicit rules with checkable results. Ambiguous items can receive suggestions, but resolution and corrective journals remain gated.

in_practice.trigger: A bank statement, subledger export or scheduled ledger snapshot becomes available.
steps: Import source records and verify completeness against source control totals.
Apply exact and approved one-to-many matching rules without altering source transactions.
Create an exception list with age, value, owner and supporting references.
Suggest possible matches or corrections while keeping uncertain items open.
Record approved resolutions and produce the reconciliation for scheduled sign-off.
in_practice.human_gate: People review ambiguous matches and every corrective posting. Material account reconciliations retain the required accountant or Controller sign-off.
data_needed: Complete bank, ledger and relevant subledger transaction sets.
Payroll and agency control totals with period identifiers.
Approved matching rules, tolerances and account ownership.
Outstanding-item history and supporting evidence.
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS reconciliation references and a restricted SharePoint register showing source totals, rule versions, matches, open items and approvals.

evidence.claim: Exact and rule-based transaction matching can run deterministically while ambiguous matches remain exceptions.
Saving 65% of handling time and completing reconciliations 2.2 times faster depends on match rates and exception ageing that have not been measured.

risks: Loose amount or date tolerances can hide real discrepancies by matching unrelated transactions.
Missing source rows can create a false impression that an account is reconciled.
Incorrect handling of reversals and split payments can count transactions twice.
Automated matching must preserve source records and a reproducible audit trail.
research_questions: What proportion of historical items match exactly, through approved grouping rules or only through judgment?
Which accounts contain the oldest or most material unexplained balances?
Can source exports prove completeness with transaction counts and control totals?
Does a historical replay reproduce approved reconciliations without concealing known errors?

tasks.short: Check whether our accounting processes work well and follow the agreed controls.

today.trigger: A recurring error, audit finding, slow close or scheduled process review prompts an inspection.
steps: Read procedures, approval rules and prior findings.
Trace sample transactions through AFAS and their supporting records.
Compare the documented process with how staff actually work.
Assess delays, control gaps and compliance with accounting procedures.
Discuss findings and agree improvements with the Controller and process owners.
drudgery: Collecting process documents and transaction samples.
Reconstructing approval paths.
Drafting repeated findings and action trackers.
today.time_sinks: Assumed workflow: evidence collection and understanding undocumented workarounds take longer than producing the final findings.

lenses.faster: Assemble process evidence and test transaction samples against agreed rules automatically. Start the review with observed failures and unanswered questions.
lenses.autonomous: Scheduled checks identify missing approvals, late postings and unusual access combinations where records support them. The accountant decides whether an alert represents a real control weakness.
lenses.ambitious: Test selected controls across the full transaction population each month. Compare the three sites and show which changes reduce errors and close delays.
lenses.joy: Remove document hunting and repetitive sample checking. Keep conversations about why workarounds exist and how to make controls practical.
lenses.options: Compare a rule change, workflow change and training intervention for each finding. Show implementation effort, control coverage and likely effect on close time.
lenses.altitude: Become the owner of continuous control assessment and improvement priorities. Judge control effectiveness using evidence of failures and their consequences.
reach: Controller: recurring operational control reviews.
Bookkeeper: design of simpler posting and approval procedures.
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: joint checks on payroll-to-finance data handoffs.

tasks.human_edge: Understand why staff bypass a procedure and judge whether a proposed control will work on busy shifts. Maintain independent judgment when reviewing processes the accountant helped design.
tasks.pattern_why: Software can collect evidence and test explicit controls, but effectiveness depends on interviews, context and professional judgment. The accountant leads the assessment and recommendation.

in_practice.trigger: A scheduled control review or a recurring exception reaches the agreed escalation threshold.
steps: Agree the review scope, control objectives and required evidence.
Gather procedures, transaction samples and available approval or access records.
Run explicit control tests and draft findings linked to their evidence.
Validate findings through walkthroughs with the people doing the work.
Agree actions, owners and measures, then check whether the changes improve outcomes.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant validates each finding and recommendation; the Controller approves control changes, with IT and relevant process owners reviewing access or workflow changes.
data_needed: Approved procedures and control objectives.
Transaction histories and available approval timestamps.
Role permissions and separation-of-duties rules.
Prior findings, exceptions and close performance measures.
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint control-review register with evidence links, validated findings, decisions, action owners and follow-up results.

evidence.claim: Explicit control testing and evidence assembly can be automated; assessing operating effectiveness still requires contextual review.
A 40% handling-time saving and 1.5-fold completion speed are untested planning estimates.

risks: Documented procedures may differ from actual practice, making automated conclusions misleading.
Incomplete approval or access logs limit what can be established.
Individual activity data could become employee monitoring; assess AVG/GDPR and applicable OR consent requirements before changing monitoring arrangements.
Reviewing one's own designs can weaken independence; material controls need separate review.
research_questions: Which AFAS approval and access records are available at sufficient detail for control testing?
Which recurring failures have a measurable effect on close time or audit adjustments?
Do walkthroughs at all three sites confirm or contradict the recorded process?
What review independence and OR involvement are required for the proposed changes?

tasks.short: Prepare accruals, corrections and other journals for the monthly close.

today.trigger: A close checklist item, reconciliation difference or late cost requires an adjusting journal.
steps: Collect schedules, contracts, invoices and payroll or agency cost evidence.
Calculate the adjustment and select accounts, sites and reporting periods.
Prepare a balanced journal with an explanation and supporting documents.
Obtain review and post the authorised journal in AFAS.
Check the posted result and schedule any required reversal.
drudgery: Rebuilding recurring accrual calculations.
Copying journal lines into AFAS.
Checking reversal dates and locating prior-month support.
today.time_sinks: Assumed workflow: recurring calculations are repetitive; incomplete evidence and unusual estimates drive the remaining review effort.

lenses.faster: Use approved templates to calculate recurring journals, validate dimensions and attach evidence. Eliminate spreadsheet rebuilding and journal re-entry.
lenses.autonomous: The close schedule generates draft accruals and reversals from current source data. Approved journals can then be imported or posted through a controlled route.
lenses.ambitious: Refresh material accrual estimates during the month so the forecast reflects costs already incurred. Compare estimates with later invoices to improve the calculation rules.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive journal construction and reversal tracking. Keep the judgment about uncertain costs and correct accounting treatment.
lenses.options: Show low, central and high estimates for uncertain agency or other costs. Explain which assumptions drive the difference and the effect on site results.
lenses.altitude: Own the journal policy, estimation methods and evidence standards. Focus on estimate accuracy and recurring causes of late corrections.
reach: Bookkeeper: preparation of recurring correcting entries.
Controller: maintenance of accrual methods and journal controls.
FP&A Analyst: current accrued costs and uncertainty ranges for forecasts.

tasks.human_edge: Decide whether a cost belongs in the period and whether an estimate is supportable. Recognise exceptional transactions that do not fit a recurring template.
tasks.pattern_why: deterministic_software should calculate approved journal templates and validate postings. An agent can gather evidence and draft explanations, but each journal needs authorisation before it affects the ledger.

in_practice.trigger: A scheduled close item becomes due or an approved reconciliation issue requires a journal.
steps: Retrieve the approved journal template, source evidence and applicable period.
Calculate the entry and expose any missing inputs or estimation assumptions.
Validate balance, account dimensions, duplicate keys, period status and reversal settings.
Present the journal and evidence to the required reviewer.
Post or import the approved entry, verify its AFAS identifier and track any reversal.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant approves estimates and treatment; a separate authorised reviewer approves postings according to journal limits. Material or unusual entries go to the Controller.
systems: Controlled Excel templates or calculation scripts
data_needed: Approved journal templates and accounting policies.
Contracts, approved hours, received invoices and other accrual evidence.
Account and site dimensions, open periods and authorisation limits.
Prior estimates, actual settlements and reversal instructions.
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS journal records linked to a restricted SharePoint evidence pack containing inputs, calculations, assumptions, approvals and reversal status.

evidence.claim: Recurring journal calculations, balance checks and reversal schedules can be represented as deterministic rules.
Saving 70% of handling time and completing journals 2.5 times faster assumes a large recurring-template share and timely approvals.

risks: Correct arithmetic can still produce a wrong journal if source evidence, period or accounting treatment is wrong.
Retries can create duplicate postings unless each journal has a unique submission key and confirmed status.
Poorly supported accrual assumptions can bias results and forecasts.
Payroll support may expose unnecessary employee details; use aggregate totals where possible.
research_questions: What percentage of journals follows stable templates, and which requires fresh judgment?
Can AFAS validate and import drafts without bypassing authorisation or period controls?
How accurate were prior agency and payroll accruals against later actuals?
Does a shadow close reproduce approved journals and catch duplicate or reversal errors?

tasks.short: Coordinate who supplies, checks and files financial records before our deadlines.

today.trigger: A close deadline, audit request or missing financial record requires coordinated work.
steps: Identify required records and assign work to bookkeepers and other record owners.
Explain deadlines, formats and evidence requirements.
Check progress and chase missing or incomplete submissions.
Resolve blockers, reprioritise work and arrange review.
Confirm records are complete, correctly filed and available to authorised reviewers.
drudgery: Sending repeated reminders.
Maintaining parallel status lists.
Checking filenames, locations and missing attachments.
today.time_sinks: Assumed workflow: status collection and chasing are repetitive; resolving workload conflicts and blockers requires personal coordination.

lenses.faster: Use one shared queue with named owners, deadlines and evidence requirements. Generate status updates from completed checks and submitted files.
lenses.autonomous: Due dates and missing submissions trigger reminders and escalation under agreed rules. Record completeness checks run when documents arrive.
lenses.ambitious: Coordinate one consistent evidence process across all three sites and maintain audit-ready records throughout the year. Identify recurring blockers before they delay the close.
lenses.joy: Remove chasing and status copying. Keep coaching colleagues, clearing blockers and agreeing priorities.
lenses.options: Compare work sequences when a deadline slips and show which close milestones each sequence protects. Let the accountant choose based on capacity and business importance.
lenses.altitude: Design the finance evidence workflow and its service expectations. Manage recurring bottlenecks rather than individual reminders.
reach: Controller: administration of the close calendar and evidence tracker.
Bookkeeper: shared filing and submission standards.
Payroll Specialist: coordination of payroll close evidence and handoff deadlines.

tasks.human_edge: Set fair priorities, understand workload and handle disagreement or sensitive feedback. Staff leadership remains personal even when routine coordination is automated.
tasks.pattern_why: deterministic_software can manage reminders, status and filing checks. The earlier automate label fits administration, but directing people and resolving priority conflicts require a human lead.

in_practice.trigger: The close calendar opens a work item, evidence arrives or an agreed deadline is missed.
steps: Create work items from approved checklists with owners, dependencies and deadlines.
Check submissions for required files, metadata and access permissions.
Update status and send authorised internal reminders through the agreed workflow.
Draft escalation summaries and alternative sequences when work is blocked.
Have the accountant resolve conflicts and confirm completion of critical evidence.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant approves assignments, changes in priority and sensitive escalations. Automated reminders follow an agreed policy and do not make judgments about individual performance.
data_needed: Close calendar, evidence checklist and dependencies.
Named owners, agreed deadlines and escalation rules.
Submission locations, required metadata and access groups.
Declared availability and workload constraints needed for coordination.
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint work register recording assignments, submission checks, reminders, escalations and human priority decisions.

evidence.claim: Shared task registers and rule-based reminders can reduce coordination administration; they do not replace personnel leadership.
A 40% handling-time saving and 1.4-fold completion speed are assumptions that depend on current chasing effort and colleague response times.

risks: Incorrect completion signals can mark evidence ready when its substance has not been reviewed.
Excessive reminders can increase interruption and create duplicate work.
Employee-level tracking requires AVG/GDPR controls and assessment of applicable OR consent rights.
Extending AI into individual performance evaluation or task allocation based on personal characteristics could bring EU AI Act high-risk employment requirements into scope.
research_questions: How much time is spent on reminders and status administration versus actual supervision?
Can one shared register replace the existing spreadsheets and mail threads?
Do reminders reduce late submissions without increasing interruptions?
What staff-data use, OR involvement and escalation rules are acceptable for this workflow?

tasks.short: Maintain our chart of accounts and map transactions to the right accounts and sites.

today.trigger: A new transaction type, supplier, reporting requirement or site cost needs a mapping or account change.
steps: Review the transaction, reporting need and existing chart of accounts.
Select the correct account, VAT treatment and site or cost dimensions.
Propose a new account or mapping when existing options are insufficient.
Obtain approval and update AFAS configuration or mapping guidance.
Check sample postings and document the effective change.
drudgery: Looking up previous classifications.
Maintaining duplicate mapping tables.
Checking whether reports use the latest account structure.
today.time_sinks: Assumed workflow: routine classification is repetitive, while new accounts and changes to reporting structure require careful review.

lenses.faster: Apply approved supplier and transaction mappings automatically. Suggest classifications for new items using the account definitions and comparable approved postings.
lenses.autonomous: Known transaction types receive their approved mapping during intake. Unknown types and requests for new accounts enter a review queue.
lenses.ambitious: Keep site and cost categories consistent enough to compare logistics costs across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo. Detect classification drift before it distorts the forecast.
lenses.joy: Remove repeated account lookups and mapping-table maintenance. Keep designing a useful account structure and resolving unusual classifications.
lenses.options: Show candidate accounts and the reporting consequences of each. Compare adding an account with using an existing account plus a cost dimension.
lenses.altitude: Own the accounting taxonomy and its change rules. Measure classification quality and whether the structure supports business decisions.
reach: Bookkeeper: routine account and cost-dimension classification.
Controller: governance of the chart of accounts.
FP&A Analyst: consistent mappings from ledger accounts to forecast categories.

tasks.human_edge: Choose account structures that preserve accounting meaning and support useful reporting. Approve treatment of novel transactions and changes that affect historical comparability.
tasks.pattern_why: Approved classifications are reusable rules and should run without a model. llm_step can suggest mappings for unfamiliar descriptions, while new accounts and rule changes require approval.

in_practice.trigger: A transaction needs classification or a proposed reporting change requires an account review.
steps: Apply the effective approved mapping to known transaction types.
Validate allowed account, VAT and site-dimension combinations.
For unknown items, suggest candidate mappings with definitions and comparable approved examples.
Route new accounts and changed rules to the accountant and Controller for approval.
Publish versioned mappings and check affected AFAS postings and Power BI reports.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant reviews unfamiliar classifications; the Controller approves chart changes. Only approved rules may classify transactions automatically, and classification alone does not authorise posting.
data_needed: Chart of accounts with definitions and permitted dimension combinations.
Approved supplier and transaction mappings with effective dates.
VAT treatment rules and historical approved examples.
Power BI and forecast category mappings.
in_practice.logs_to: A versioned SharePoint mapping register linked to AFAS configuration changes, approvals and affected reporting definitions.

evidence.claim: Stable account mappings can run as explicit rules, with model suggestions reserved for descriptions that do not match those rules.
A 60% handling-time saving and 1.8-fold completion speed depend on the share of recurring classifications and are untested.

risks: Historical postings may contain errors that a suggestion system repeats.
Supplier-only rules can misclassify suppliers providing several kinds of goods or services.
Account changes can break Power BI measures and reduce comparability with prior periods.
Automatic account creation can cause uncontrolled growth of the chart.
research_questions: What share of classifications is stable enough for rules rather than suggestions?
Are account definitions, dimension rules and forecast mappings complete and consistent?
Which historical classifications are suitable as approved reference examples?
Can a proposed chart change be tested against all affected reports before activation?

tasks.short: Improve and document our AFAS accounting workflows and the links to reporting and bank systems.

today.trigger: A control gap, manual workaround, reporting need or system change requires a workflow improvement.
steps: Describe the problem and map the current records, controls and handoffs.
Agree requirements with Finance, IT and affected payroll or site owners.
Design configuration, imports, validations or reporting changes.
Test representative cases and failure handling outside production.
Obtain approval, release the change and document operation and ownership.
drudgery: Writing repetitive specifications and operating instructions.
Preparing sample data and test cases.
Maintaining manual exports and spreadsheet handoffs.
today.time_sinks: Assumed workflow: understanding integration limits, coordinating owners and validating safe changes take more time than drafting documentation.

lenses.faster: Use AI to draft specifications, validation scripts and operating instructions from an agreed process. Reuse tested components for imports, reconciliations and exception queues.
lenses.autonomous: Approved integrations can run on schedules and report failed imports or changed data formats. Design choices and production releases stay with named owners.
lenses.ambitious: Replace fragile spreadsheet handoffs with reproducible data flows that feed both the close and forecast. Make recurring controls run during the month rather than only at month-end.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive documentation and small amounts of repetitive coding. Keep solving process problems and seeing fewer errors reach colleagues.
lenses.options: Compare AFAS configuration, a Microsoft 365 workflow and a small custom integration. Show operating cost, controls, maintenance needs and recovery arrangements.
lenses.altitude: Become the finance process and data-control owner. Set standards for interfaces, evidence, exception handling and safe change.
reach: Controller: design and maintenance of finance controls.
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: specifications for payroll-to-finance interfaces.
FP&A Analyst: reliable actuals feeds and reporting definitions.
IT application support: finance acceptance criteria and operational runbooks.

tasks.human_edge: Translate accounting obligations into system requirements and decide whether a design is safe and usable. Coordinate ownership and acceptance across Finance, IT and the sites.
tasks.pattern_why: AI can help create specifications, code and documentation, but system design and acceptance require accounting and operational judgment. The resulting routine workflows should use deterministic_software wherever rules are sufficient.

in_practice.trigger: An approved improvement request identifies a measurable accounting problem.
steps: Define the outcome, current effort, control requirements and accountable owners.
Compare implementation options against confirmed interface and permission limits.
Draft configuration, code and documentation in a development environment using synthetic or minimised data.
Test totals, permissions, duplicate handling, failure recovery and representative accounting cases.
Obtain Finance and IT acceptance, release through change control and monitor the agreed outcome.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant approves accounting behaviour; IT reviews security and operation; the Controller or designated owner authorises production release. Bank and ledger permissions remain subject to separation of duties.
systems: AFAS Profit test environment and approved interfaces
Rabobank approved interfaces or test files
data_needed: Current process maps, requirements and measured error or handling rates.
Confirmed AFAS, Microsoft 365 and bank interface specifications.
Accounting controls, access roles and retention requirements.
Representative test cases, source control totals and recovery procedures.
in_practice.logs_to: The approved change register and version-control repository, linked to SharePoint requirements, acceptance evidence, release decisions and operational runbooks.

evidence.claim: AI can assist with specifications, code and documentation; reliable accounting automation still requires interface validation, testing and accountable release decisions.
A 40% handling-time saving and 1.5-fold completion speed are untested estimates; integration constraints may reduce the gain.

risks: Generated code or configuration can look correct while mishandling totals, duplicates or failed submissions.
Unsupported interfaces and portal format changes can create ongoing maintenance work.
Development access can accidentally bypass production accounting controls.
Sending live payroll or supplier data to unapproved AI services can breach confidentiality and AVG/GDPR obligations.
research_questions: Which interfaces, test environments and workflow licences are actually available?
Which manual handoff has enough recurring cost or error impact to justify maintenance?
Can the proposed design recover from partial failure without duplicate ledger or payment actions?
Who will own support, monitoring and updates after release?

role.altitude: The accountant becomes the owner of reliable ledger flows, reconciliations and close evidence, spending more time on exceptions, accounting judgment and prevention.
reach: Bookkeeper: routine invoice checks, transaction classification and reconciliation administration.
Controller: continuous control testing, close coordination and accrual governance.
FP&A Analyst: reconciled actuals, current accrual estimates and explanations that improve forecast trust.
Payroll Specialist and People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: controlled payroll-to-ledger handoffs and aggregate reconciliations.
IT application support: finance requirements, acceptance testing and operating standards for accounting interfaces.
role.ceiling_note: These eight tasks total 664.2 hours per FTE annually, about 41.5% of a 1,600-hour role. The proposed savings total about 369 hours per FTE, or 739 hours across two FTE, before overlap, implementation and maintenance; at EUR 70/hour this is about EUR 51,700 of annual capacity value, not assured cash savings. Workflows and estimates are inferred, not observed; time_saved_pct estimates human handling time, while speedup estimates elapsed task completion including remaining waits. Accounting judgment, approvals, staff leadership and cross-team response times limit further gains, and the rest of the role has not been assessed.
skills_to_grow: Translate accounting policies and controls into explicit, testable rules.
Use AFAS extracts, Excel and basic SQL to validate completeness and trace balances.
Design approval gates, separation of duties and reproducible evidence trails.
Review AI-generated explanations and code against source evidence.
Measure exception rates, accrual accuracy, audit adjustments and close delays.
Manage process changes with Finance, IT, payroll and site owners, including AVG/GDPR and applicable OR requirements.
role.ambitious_version: Run a continuously checked ledger across the three sites, with routine matches and drafts prepared automatically and material exceptions resolved by people. Deliver earlier reconciled actuals and better accrual evidence to the Controller and FP&A, then demonstrate a shorter close and a forecast the business trusts.
